newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW-NZ employment growth well above fcast.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-NZ employment growth well above fcast.

text.p: The following are economists' initial reactions to New Zealand employment data released on Friday.

Statistics New Zealand said unemployment was a seasonally adjusted 6.3 percent in the September quarter. Employment rose a seasonally adjusted 0.8 percent in the quarter and 3.7 percent in the year to September.

Economists had forecast an unemployment rate of 6.23 percent for the September quarter. Their consensus forecasts were for employment growth of 0.24 percent for the quarter aand 2.84 percent for the year.
DAVID PLANK, CHIEF ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST

"It was obviously a lot stronger then the market and the Reserve Bank would have been looking for. The RB was looking for 1.2 percent employment growth in the year to March. It has now had 1.7 percent in the first six months of that year. We need to look at hours worked to see what has happened to output. Negative for bonds initially."

"Obviously it (employment growth) continued to be strong. On the surface that is not an encouraging result for the Reserve Bank. Having said that, a lot of that growth appears to be in part time employment. So I think they will be looking closely at the wages data due in the next couple of weeks. At this stage it doesn't fundamentally change the outlook for monetary policy. Slightly negative for bonds."
